active_themes.label: Warsh's First Decision—Hawkish
active_themes.summary: Warsh held rates steady and signaled possible hikes before year-end, rejecting the market's assumption of imminent cuts. This was the exact opposite of the 'maximum cover' scenario described six weeks ago—Warsh chose credibility over political cover. The market heard 'hold' and immediately pivoted to Iran relief instead of repricing into the hike signal. Equities did not materially reprice because geopolitical euphoria dominated the narrative. This repricing will arrive when credit stress forces lenders to act, not when headlines relieve it.

active_themes.label: Iran Deal Announcement—Temporary
active_themes.summary: Trump announced a formal deal framework today, collapsing oil from $82 to below $80 in hours. This is genuine relief but has a known half-life of 3-7 days without concrete sanctions relief and nuclear agreement terms. The market's critical error: treating oil relief as inflation relief when 4.2% inflation is now decoupled from energy and rooted in sticky wage/consumption dynamics. Spending growth remains flat at 0%. Oil will retest $82+ within the week as deal details stall or Iran escalates.

active_themes.label: Lender Silence Extends—Breaks Within Days
active_themes.summary: Discover, Capital One, and Amex had maximum cover today (stagflation backdrop, Iran relief, Warsh's policy error signaling margin compression ahead) to announce deposit rate cuts or credit tightening. All remained silent. This silence is deliberate—lenders are waiting for geopolitical euphoria to fade before triggering margin pressure announcements. Within 3-7 days, as Iran talks stall and oil stabilizes, lenders will move. That move cascades directly into equity repricing.

active_themes.label: Soft Landing Dead—Confirmed
active_themes.summary: Today's 1.21% equity decline on a hawkish Fed signal masked by Iran relief proves equities have not repriced into stagflation. The repricing trigger is lender action (credit tightening or deposit rate cuts), not geopolitical headlines. Warsh's signal to hike before year-end + zero spending growth + 4.2% inflation = the Fed is cutting rates into demand destruction. Equities are wrong by approximately 8-12% based on historical stagflation scenarios.

active_themes.label: Yields Correct—Holding the Stagflation Price
active_themes.summary: The 10-year remained flat at 3.9-4.1% despite the Iran rally and Warsh's hawkish hold. This is exactly correct: the bond market is pricing stagflation (Fed cuts into inflation, demand collapses). Equities rallied on geopolitical relief; bonds understood that the spending path and inflation trajectory have not changed. Yields will not move lower without hard evidence of demand destruction, which credit tightening will provide.

active_themes.label: Bonds Price Correctly—Equities Wrong
active_themes.summary: The flat yield response to today's combination (Warsh hike signal + Iran relief + 0% spending) confirms bonds understand the scenario better than equities. Warsh just signaled he will hike into 4.2% inflation and 0% spending growth—textbook demand destruction setup. Bonds held firm; equities rallied on oil relief and missed the signal entirely.

active_themes.label: Lender Silence—Timing the Announcement
active_themes.summary: Today's geopolitical relief gave lenders the cover they needed to delay announcing margin pressure. They will break that silence within 3-7 days when Iran euphoria fades and oil stabilizes back above $82. That announcement (deposit rate cuts or credit tightening) is the trigger that reprices equities from the 1.21% loss they should have taken today into the 8-12% repricing the stagflation scenario demands.

active_themes.label: Soft Landing Dead
active_themes.summary: Today's rally proves equities have not repriced into stagflation—they rallied on a temporary oil relief story instead of repricing into demand destruction. This is the last repricing window before lenders force the issue. May's 0% spending growth + 4.2% inflation + today's rally + Warsh's policy error = equities are wrong, and will correct when credit tightens, not when oil rises again.

active_themes.label: Warsh Chose Credibility Over Politics
active_themes.summary: The new Fed chair rejected the assumption that he would cut or hold silently. He explicitly signaled hikes before year-end, telegraphing that he understands 4.2% inflation cannot be cut away without demand destruction. This is a credibility play—Warsh is signaling he will not be a political Fed. The market has not yet priced the implications of a hawkish Fed in a 0% spending growth environment.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks above 4.1% or 30-year stays at/exceeds 2007 highs for more than 3 consecutive trading days
open_watchlist.meaning: Stagflation expectations are hardening; equities will compress into margin compression and demand destruction risks, regardless of geopolitical relief.

open_watchlist.condition: Capital One, Discover, or American Express announces deposit rate cuts and/or tightens consumer credit standards
open_watchlist.meaning: Lender paralysis has broken and equities will reprice 8-15% lower into demand destruction and margin compression within one week.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks above 4.1% and stays there for 3+ consecutive trading days
open_watchlist.meaning: Bond market is rejecting the de-escalation relief narrative and repricing stagflation risk; equities follow with 5-8% selloff as multiple compression accelerates.

open_watchlist.condition: Capital One, Discover, or American Express announces deposit rate cuts or tightens consumer credit standards
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the repricing trigger. When lenders move, equities will recognize that the Fed is cutting into stagflation, not into a recoverable economy.

open_watchlist.condition: Capital One, Discover, or American Express announces deposit rate cuts or tightens consumer credit standards within 7 days
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the cascade trigger: lender action forces margin compression and demand destruction into a flat-spending backdrop, confirming stagflation scenario and equities repricing lower.

open_watchlist.condition: Iran talks stall or Iran escalates rhetoric beyond June 22; oil moves back above $82
open_watchlist.meaning: Geopolitical relief narrative collapses, equities lose their cover story, and the focus returns immediately to Warsh's decision and lender credit tightening.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks above 4.1% and holds there for 3+ consecutive trading days despite Warsh's decision
open_watchlist.meaning: Bonds are signaling that rate cuts are not coming or are too shallow to matter; stagflation pricing is firm and equities will follow lower.

open_watchlist.condition: Oil moves back above $82 or Iran deal talks stall before June 25
open_watchlist.meaning: This signals Iran relief is temporary and geopolitical risk is returning. Combined with lender tightening, this confirms demand destruction is the base case and equities reprice sharply.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks above 4.1% and holds for 3+ consecutive trading days despite Warsh's hold
open_watchlist.meaning: This would signal the bond market is repricing upward into higher-for-longer rates (not cuts), confirming equities have misread Warsh's signal and stagflation is the correct scenario.

open_watchlist.condition: Another Fed official (Barkin, Powell, etc.) publicly reinforces Warsh's hike signal or warns of stagflation risks
open_watchlist.meaning: This would confirm Warsh is not an outlier and the entire Fed is ready to tighten into demand destruction, accelerating equity repricing and lender action.
